It shall be the duty of all owners and tenants of all houses and structures in the city to obtain from the city manager the correct number assigned to his house or structure, and thereafter to post the assigned number in a conspicuous place on the house or structure, or on the property, so that the same may be seen from the street.
(Code 1975, § 38-11)
Cross reference— Buildings and building regulations, Ch. 6.
930:
The building inspector is hereby prohibited from issuing any permit for the construction of any house of any kind to any person until a number shall have been assigned to such structure by the city manager.
(Code 1975, § 38-12)
Cross reference— Buildings and building regulations, Ch. 6.
931:
No person shall erect any drain, gutter, downspout, valley or any flat or sloping roof of any character that will in any manner drain or shed water on any sidewalk of the city.
(Code 1975, § 38-13)
932:
It shall be unlawful for any person to place or cause to be placed in any street or alley, any dirt, trash or other material so as to interfere with the drainage or use of the street or alley, without first obtaining a permit to do so from the city manager.
(Code 1975, § 38-14)
933:
(a) No person shall cause any water or other liquids to be disposed of on the streets or sidewalks of the city without the written permission of the city council.
(b) The terms of this section shall not be applicable to the members of the fire department or any officer, agent, or employee of the city in the performance of a designated municipal duty.
(Code 1975, § 38-15)
934:
It shall be the duty of all occupants of improved property and owners of vacant property, in front of which the sidewalks have been paved, to keep such sidewalks clean, and to do such sweeping and scraping as may be necessary to remove clay, dirt and trash therefrom, and to render the same passable, comfortable and sightly. In addition, it shall be the duty of the city manager, after five days' written notice to any such person of the necessity for cleaning such sidewalk, to have done such work as may be necessary to render such walk clean and to render a bill covering the cost of such cleaning to the owner or agent of such property in person, or if such person or agent be a nonresident, then by mail. Upon the nonpayment of such bill within ten (10) days after service of same as aforesaid, the city clerk shall issue an execution therefor against the owner of the abutting property and such execution shall be a lien upon such property and shall be collected as other executions issued by the city.
(Code 1975, § 38-16)
Cross reference— Health and sanitation, Ch. 12.
937:
It shall be unlawful for any person to dig or excavate in any public place within the city or install, repair or replace any of his property or equipment in such public place, or do any other work in or on any public place, which requires the removal or breaking of the surface or underpart of any such public place, unless and until such person shall have first secured, in the manner provided in this article, permission to do so.
(Code 1975, § 38-20)
938:
Each person desiring permission to dig or excavate in any public place shall file with the city manager a written or printed application, setting forth the character and location of such work to be done in any such public place, the probable number of square yards of surface to be removed and the probable date of beginning and the completion of the work.
(Code 1975, § 38-21)
939:
If the applicant for the permit to excavate is authorized to perform the work himself, including replacing the street to its condition prior to the excavation, there shall be no charge for the issuance of the permit. If the city must fill and resurface the street or public way, the applicant shall deposit with the city at the time of application, a sum of money which shall be fixed by the city manager and shall be based on the cost per square yard of replacement plus ten (10) percent.
(Code 1975, § 38-22)
940:
Each application, as referred to in section 19-22 shall be considered by the city manager, who shall then, without unreasonable delay, either grant or reject such application. Upon rejection of the application, the applicant shall have the right to present the matter to the city council, the order of which shall be final in such matter, and upon final rejection, the deposit of money referred to in section 19-23 shall be returned to the person who deposited the same.
(Code 1975, § 38-23)
941:
Upon the failure of any person, whose application to dig or excavate shall have been granted and who shall have begun the work, to complete the same without delay, or upon the completion of such work, to restore the public place to the same or as good a condition as the same was before such work was done, or to comply with any reasonable rules or regulations of the superintendent of streets from time to time given to such person for the completion and restoration of such public place, such person shall upon conviction, in addition to other penalties, forfeit to the city any deposit of money so made with the city.
(Code 1975, § 38-24)
942:
Upon the failure of any person to make such repairs as herein required in the manner or in the time required, the city manager is empowered and authorized to cause such repairs to be made and such public place to be restored to its original condition, and the cost thereof, plus ten (10) percent thereof, shall be charged to and paid by such person who so failed to make such repairs, and such sum of money shall constitute and be a debt due from such person to the city.
(Code 1975, § 38-25)
943:
The deposit of money made under section 19-23 shall stand as a guarantee and may be employed by the city for the replacement of such public place in as good condition as the same was immediately before the excavation or digging, and upon default of the person so making such deposit to restore immediately the public place to as good condition as the same was immediately before such excavation or digging was done by him, the city manager may employ the whole or any part of such deposit of money necessary for such restoration. Upon the restoration of the public place to such condition as the same was immediately before such digging or excavating, the city clerk shall, upon the certificate of the city manager, restore to the person so making such deposit such sum of money so deposited, or in case any part thereof is employed by the city for such restoration of such public place, upon such certificate, the city clerk shall refund such part of such sum of money so remaining.
(Code 1975, § 38-26)
944:
All digging or excavating to be done, as provided in this article, shall be promptly started and completed without delay after permission shall have been granted, and such public place shall be, immediately upon the completion of such work, restored to the same or as good condition as the same was before such work was done thereon. Such work or restoration shall be at all times and in all respects in compliance with the orders and supervision of the superintendent of streets from time to time given to such person for such purpose.
(Code 1975, § 38-27)
945:
Upon the granting of an application for permission to dig or excavate in any public place, and in all other cases provided for in this chapter, it shall be the duty of the applicant, before beginning any such work, to enclose the place where such work is being done or otherwise afford adequate protection to street traffic. He shall post and keep posted at such place a placard showing that the work is being done under a permit granted by the city, with sufficient other information thereon to give ample warning to those using such public place that the same is out of repair or being repaired, and in addition thereto, he shall place sufficient markings at night by a red or amber light, to notify those having the right to use the same that such public place, or part thereof, is closed.
(Code 1975, § 38-28)
946:
Any controversy between the person making a deposit in order to dig or excavate in any public place and the superintendent of streets or the city manager, respecting any of the duties to be performed by any of them, may be submitted to the city council by any of the parties, and when so submitted, the action of the city council thereon shall be binding on all the parties.
(Code 1975, § 38-29)
949:
(a) Any action to either open or close a street or alley or any portion thereof within the city limits shall be initiated either by the city council, upon its own motion, or by petition of all abutting property owners of the portion of the street or alley to be opened or closed, the petition to be filed with the city clerk and brought before the mayor and council at its next meeting, either regular or called.
(b) At the meeting of the mayor and council, if such action is recommended by motion of any member of the city council, the same shall be read and tabled for action at the next regular meeting, or if such action is initiated by petition, the petition shall be read and tabled for action at the next regular meeting, and at the next regular meeting evidence shall be heard, if presented, and the determination of the city council made at such time and spread upon the minutes. The city council may table final determination until the next regular meeting, if it so desires, and if the same is so tabled, it shall not be necessary to republish the public notice provided in section 18-47.
(Code 1975, § 38-30)
950:
Between the time of the first reading of the motion or petition to open or close a street or alley or any portion thereof, and the next regular meeting of the city council, the clerk of the city shall cause to be published in a newspaper of general circulation in the city a notice to the public of the proposed opening or closing of a street or alley or any portion thereof, and the time and place of the meeting at which a determination of such matter shall be made by the city council. Such public notice shall be published in such newspaper once a week for four (4) weeks immediately preceding the meeting at which said determination is to be made.
(Code 1975, § 38-31)
951:
The cost of any such proceeding, including all advertising costs, shall be borne by the city if the same is initiated upon motion of the city council, and the cost thereof shall be borne by the petitioner if the same is initiated by petition of abutting property owners, the cost to be paid to the city at the time of the filing of the petition.
(Code 1975, § 38-32)
952:
If any street or alley or portion thereof is closed under this procedure, the same shall not be considered abandoned, and any such action shall not be construed as an abandonment by the city. There shall be no abandonment of any street or portion thereof unless the city council shall specifically declare a street or any portion thereof "abandoned" in a properly passed resolution.
(Code 1975, § 38-33)
953:
The title to streets or alleys closed by such action shall remain in the city unless sold as herein provided for. The city may either use the property for public purposes; hold title thereto and reopen the same as a public street or alley, if the city council shall in the future determine to do the same; or may sell the property to the abutting property owners, the centerline of said street or alley to be the dividing line, at the fair and reasonable market value of the property at the time of such sale.
(Code 1975, § 38-34)
956:
It shall be unlawful for anyone to cut or construct a street or lane belonging to the city, or to cause the same to be cut or constructed without first obtaining a permit from the building inspector of the city.
(Code 1975, § 38-40)
958:
No permit for cutting or constructing any street or lane shall be issued for any street or lane which is to be dedicated to the public or is to become a part of the system of city streets unless the same meets all of the right-of-way requirements and paving and base requirements of the city.
(Code 1975, § 38-42)
959:
For the purposes of this article any street or lane on which more than two (2) dwelling units or more than two (2) business establishments or more than two (2) manufacturing establishments or any combination of the aforesaid totaling more than two (2) shall be located shall be presumed to be a public street or lane.
(Code 1975, § 38-43)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, § 1-2.
960:
No building permit shall be issued for any construction for new dwellings or buildings or expansion of existing dwellings or buildings on any street or lane which exists in violation of this article or any portion hereof.
(Code 1975, § 38-44)
Cross reference— Buildings and building regulations, Ch. 6.
961:
The denial of a street permit by the building inspector or the denial of a building permit by the building inspector due to violations of this article may be appealed directly to the mayor and council. Any such appeal must be in writing, must have attached thereto a copy of the application which has been previously filed with the building inspector, and must be delivered to the city clerk at the city hall not later than ten (10) days after the denial of the street permit or building permit. The appeal must state clearly the name and address of the appellant, and the telephone, if any, of the appellant. The mayor and council must conduct a public hearing on the appeal within forty-five (45) days from the date the appeal is filed with the city clerk, and the appellant must be notified in writing by the city clerk of the date, time and place of the hearing, it being sufficient for the purposes of this article that the notice be mailed to the appellant at the address given in the appeal by regular United States mail at least seven (7) days prior to the date set for the hearing.
(Code 1975, § 38-45)
Cross reference— Buildings and building regulations, Ch. 6.
962:
The cutting or construction of any street or lane in violation of this article or any part hereof shall constitute an offense punishable by the recorder's court.
(Code 1975, § 38-46)
963:
In addition to any criminal penalty imposed under section 19-71, the cutting or constructing of any street or lane in violation of this article or any part hereof may be enjoined in the Superior Court of Walker County, Georgia.
(Code 1975, § 38-47)
966:
This article is known as the "Regulation of Timber Harvesting Activity."
(Ord. No. 18-04, § 1, 2-12-2018)
967:
As used in this article, timber harvesting shall means the harvesting of standing timber for delivery as pulpwood, logs, poles, posts, or wood chips to any woodyard or processing plant located inside or outside this state. Such term shall not apply to landscaping or removal of dead or diseased trees from public or private property.
(Ord. No. 18-04, § 1, 2-12-2018)
968:
It is the purpose and intent of this article to protect the public streets and roads of the city from damage, including erosion and deposits of sedimentation, that often occur from timber harvesting activities. This article is enacted pursuant to the authority of a municipal corporation to regulate streets or roads within its jurisdiction in accordance with O.C.G.A. Title 32. Nothing in this article is intended to preclude the city from imposing regulations on private land use activities relating to development, such as zoning, tree protection, landscaping, or streamside buffer regulations.
(Ord. No. 18-04, § 1, 2-12-2018)
969:
(a) All timber harvesters harvesting timber in the City of LaFayette must comply with all relevant provisions of O.C.G.A. § 12-6-24 in order to use any public street or road(s) in the city for transporting harvested timber, other than a federal or state highway.
(b) An appointment for ingress/egress inspection shall be scheduled forty-eight (48) hours in advance of the commencement of activity with the public works director to allow the public works director and the codes enforcement director or their designated agents to inspect the site prior to any activity at the proposed ingress/egress location.
(c) The following minimum standards shall be met unless directed otherwise by the public works director or codes enforcement director or their respective designated agent:
(1) Use geotextile underliner minimum twenty (20) feet wide under gravel pad.
(2) Minimum drive width shall be twenty (20) feet.
(3) Minimum thickness of six (6) inches constructed of one and one-half (1½) inches to three and one-half (3½) inches of coarse aggregate for a minimum drive length of fifty (50) feet.
(4) The street or road, at each ingress/egress point, shall be posted with four (4) forty-eight-inch orange "Trucks Entering Highway" advance warning signs placed on the shoulder of the road at five hundred (500) feet and one thousand (1,000) feet intervals from both directions. Signs and posts shall conform to the current edition of the Manual for Uniform Traffic Control Devices.
(5) All tree harvesting activities shall be performed in accordance with generally accepted forestry land management practices and/or agricultural operations, not incidental to development, on tracts zoned for or used for forestry, silvicultural, or agricultural purpose.
(d) No harvester equipment or vehicle(s) may be parked on a public right-of-way or use the public right-of-way as a loading facility.
(e) Once items (a) through (c)(4) have been accomplished and notification given to the public works director or his designated agent, the timber harvester must provide the following to the public works director:
(1) Persons or firms conducting timber harvesting activities in the City of LaFayette shall furnish to the city, a surety bond in the sum of five thousand dollars ($5,000.00) in a form required by law and approved by the city attorney prior to beginning any timber harvesting activities or, at the option of the person or firm harvesting timber, a valid irrevocable letter of credit issued by a bank or savings and loan association, as defined in O.C.G.A. § 7-1-4, in the amount of and in lieu of such bond. A separate surety bond or letter of credit shall be required for each tract for which timber harvesting is to occur. In addition, a map of the area identifying the location of the tract to be harvested and the main point and any alternate points of ingress to such tract from a public road and, if different, any point of egress from such a tract to a public road. Said bond or letter of credit shall indemnify and protect the city from any damage to public street or road(s) or clean-up cost associated with any timber harvesting activity conducted.
(2) Said bond(s) or letter(s) of credit shall be valid only for the calendar year in which it is issued.
(3) Timber harvester shall submit a fully completed notice of timber harvesting activity, in the form approved by the Georgia Forestry Commission, as found on its website, along with all requested additional information and surety bond(s) or bank letter(s) of credit to the public works director, who along with the codes enforcement director, then shall review the documentation submitted and then the public works director shall notify the timber harvester of approval or denial to proceed with the timber harvesting process. It shall be the duty of the public works director to promptly provide a copy of every approved notice of timber harvesting activity to the Office of the Walker County Commissioner.
Pursuant to the soil erosion, sedimentation and pollution control ordinance, section 18.5-7(d), a citation will be issued immediately by the public works director or codes enforcement director upon proof of any sediment entering onto a public street or road or sedimentation entering any waters of the state or United States.
(Ord. No. 18-04, § 1, 2-12-2018)
970:
(a) Liability.
(1) Violation of the notice requirements of this article shall result in the immediate issuance of a stop-work order by the public works director or codes enforcement director against the timber harvester, and issuance of a citation, returnable to the Municipal Court of LaFayette, Georgia. Upon conviction, a violator shall be punished by a fine not exceeding five hundred dollars ($500.00).
(2) Neither the approval of a plan under the provisions of this article, nor the compliance with provisions of this article shall relieve any person from the responsibility for damage to any person or property otherwise imposed by the law nor impose any liability upon the city for damages to any person or property.
(3) No provision of this article shall permit any persons to violate the Georgia Erosion and Sedimentation Act of 1975, the Georgia Water Quality Control Act, any rules and regulations promulgated and approved thereunder, any local ordinance(s) enacted pursuant thereto, or to pollute any waters of the state or United States, as defined thereby.
(Ord. No. 18-04, § 1, 2-12-2018)
973:
(a) Intent and purpose. The City of LaFayette (the "city") is vitally concerned with the use, construction within, and occupancy of all rights-of-way in the city as such rights-of-way are a valuable and limited resource which must be utilized to promote the public health, safety, welfare, and economic development of the city and to protect public works infrastructure. Therefore, the city, under the authority of the Laws and Constitution of the State of Georgia including, but not limited to O.C.G.A. 32-4-92, has adopted this article for the purpose of regulating public and private entities which use the city rights-of-way.
(b) Scope. The provisions of this chapter apply to all utilities and facilities occupying the rights-of-way as provided in this article.
(c) Definitions. For the purposes of this article, the following terms, phrases, words, and their derivations, whether capitalized or lowercase, have the following meanings:
Business day is defined as defined in O.C.G.A. 25-9-3(3).
City means the City of LaFayette, Georgia.
Codified ordinances means the LaFayette City Code.
Construct means, but shall not be limited to, dig, bore, tunnel, trench, excavate, obstruct, install or remove facilities, other than landscaping or ornamental plantings, in, on, above, within, over, below, under, or through any part of the rights-of-way. Construct shall also include the act of opening or cutting into the surface of any paved or improved surface that is any part of the right-of-way.
Construction means, but shall not be limited to, the act or process of digging, boring, tunneling, trenching, excavating, obstructing, installing or removing facilities, other than landscaping or ornamental plantings, in, on, above, within, over, below, under, along or through any part of the rights-of-way. Construction shall also include the act of opening, boring or cutting into the surface of any part of the right-of-way.
Department means the City of LaFayette Public Works Department.
Director means the Public Works Director of the City of LaFayette, Georgia, or his or her designee.
Emergency means a condition that poses a clear and immediate danger to life, health, or safety of a person, or of significant damage or loss of real or personal property caused by such things as natural disasters, fire, subversive activities, and like events.
Facility or facilities means any tangible thing, including, but not limited to, pipes, mains, conduits, cables, wires, poles, signs, towers, traffic control devices and other signals, and other equipment, appurtenances, appliances and future technology of any utility in, on, above, within, over, below, under, along or through any part of the rights-of-way in the city.
Facilities representative(s) means the specifically identified agent(s)/employee(s) of a utility who are authorized to direct field activities of that utility and serve as official notice agent(s) for facilities-related information. Utility must ensure at least one (1) of its facilities representatives is available at all times to receive notice of, and immediately direct response to, facilities-related emergencies or situations;
FCC means the Federal Communications Commission or any successor agency.
Permit means an authorization which grants permission to conduct specific regulated activities in, on, above, within, over, below, under, along or through any public right-of-way, and which may be subject to conditions specified in a written agreement with the city or in a related provision of this Code of Ordinances.
Right(s)-of-way means the surface and space in, on, above, within, over, below, under or through any real property in which the city has an interest in law or equity, whether held in fee, or other estate or interest, or as a trustee for the public, including, but not limited to, any public street, boulevard, road, highway, freeway, lane, alley, court, sidewalk, parkway, or any other place, area, or real property owned by or under the legal or equitable control of the city that, now or hereafter, is consistent with the purposes for which it was dedicated, may be used for the purposes of constructing, operating, repairing or replacing facilities.
Service(s) means the offering of any service by a utility for a fee directly to the public, or to such classes of users as to be effectively available directly to the public, or alternatively, the provision of any service by a utility between two (2) or more points for a proprietary purpose to a class of users other than the general public.
Service agreement means a valid license agreement, service agreement, franchise agreement, or operating agreement issued by the city or state pursuant to law and accepted by a utility or entered into by and between the city and a utility, which allows such utility to operate or provide service within the geographic limits of the city.
Street or streets means the surface of, as well as the spaces above and below, any and all the streets, alleys, avenues, roads, bridges, tunnels and public places of the city within the corporate limits of the city, as the same now exist or may be hereafter extended or altered, and any location thereon, thereover or thereunder, and any portion thereof.
Transfer means the disposal by the utility, directly or indirectly, by gift, assignment, sale, merger, consolidation, or otherwise, of more than fifty (50) percent at one (1) time of the ownership or controlling interest in the facility, or of more than fifty (50) percent cumulatively over the term of a written approval of registration of such interests to a corporation, partnership, limited partnership, trust, or association, or person or group of persons acting in concert.
Unused facility or facilities means facilities located in the rights-of-way which have remained unused for twelve (12) months and for which the utility is unable to provide the city with a plan detailing the procedure by which the utility intends to begin actively using such facilities within the next twelve (12) months, or that it has a potential purchaser or user of the facilities who will be actively using the facilities within the next twelve (12) months, or, that the availability of such facilities is required by the utility to adequately and efficiently operate its facilities.
Utility or utilities means all privately, publicly, or cooperatively owned systems for producing, transmitting, or distributing communication, data, information, telecommunication, cable television, video services, power, electricity, light, heat, gas, oil, crude products, water/sewer, steam, fire and police signals, traffic control devices, and street lighting systems, and housing or conduit for any of the foregoing, which directly or indirectly serve the public or any part thereof. The term "utility" may also be used to refer to the owner, operator, utility, service, contractor or subcontractor, or any agent thereof, of any above-described utility or utility facility.
(Ord. No. 19-01, § 1, 1-14-2019)
974:
(a) Registration required. Each utility who occupies, uses or has facilities in the rights-of-way at the time of passage of this article, including by lease, sublease or assignment to operate facilities located in the rights-of-way, unless specifically exempted by state or federal law or this Code, must file a registration statement with the department within ninety (90) days of the effective date of this article.
(b) Registration procedure. The registration information provided to the city must be on a form approved by the city and include, but not be limited to:
(1) The name, legal status (i.e. partnership, corporation, etc.), street address, email address, and telephone and facsimile numbers of the utility filing the registration statement (the "registrant"). If the registrant is not the owner of the facility in the right-of-way, the registration must include the name, street address, email address if applicable, and telephone and facsimile numbers of the owner;
The name, street address, email address and telephone and facsimile numbers of one (1) or more facilities representative(s). Current information regarding how to contact the facilities representative(s) in an emergency must be provided at the time of filing a registration and must be updated as necessary to assure accurate contact information is available to the city at all times.
(2) A copy, if requested, of the utility's certificate of authority (or other acceptable evidence of authority to operate) from the Georgia Public Service Commission or the FCC and any other similar approvals, permits, or agreements.
(3) A copy, if requested, of the utility's certificate of authority (or other acceptable evidence of authority to operate) from the Georgia Public Service Commission or the FCC and any other similar approvals, permits, or agreements.
(4) A copy, if requested, of the service agreement or other legal instrument that authorizes the utility to use or occupy the right-of-way for the purpose described in the registration.
(c) Incomplete registration. If a registration is incomplete, the director must promptly notify the registrant and must provide a reasonable period of time in which to complete the registration. When a registration is complete, the director will accept it and so notify the utility in writing.
(d) Acceptance of the registration does not convey title in the rights-of-way. Acceptance of the registration is only the nonexclusive, limited right to occupy rights-of-way in the city for the limited purposes stated in the acceptance. Acceptance of the registration does not excuse a utility from obtaining permits required by city codes nor from obtaining appropriate access or pole attachment agreements before using the facilities of others, including the city. Acceptance of the registration does not excuse a utility from notifying the city of construction as required in this article.
(e) Facilities in place without registration. Beginning one (1) year after the effective date of this article, any facilities or part of a facility found in a right-of-way for which registration is required but has not been obtained, unless specifically exempted by law, and for which no valid service agreement exists with the city, may be deemed to be a nuisance and an unauthorized use of the rights-of-way. The city may exercise any remedies or rights it has at law or in equity, including, but not limited to abating the nuisance; taking possession of the facilities, evicting the utility from the right-of-way; prosecuting the violator; or any other remedy provided by city codes or otherwise allowed in law or in equity.
(Ord. No. 19-01, § 1, 1-14-2019)
976:
(a) Utility accommodation manual adopted. The 2016 GDOT Utility Accommodation Policy and Standards Manual, including all references contained to codes, rules, regulations, schedules, forms and appendix items, except appendix B (permit forms and supporting documents), promulgated by the State of Georgia Department of Transportation, as may be amended from time to time, is hereby adopted by reference and incorporated in this article as if fully set forth in this article, subject to the amendments and modification contained in this article. A copy of the manual will be maintained in the offices of the director or his or her designee and open for public inspection and copying. Copies of the manual are also available on the Georgia Department of Transportation's website. Any conflicts between the provisions of this article and the manual will be resolved in favor of the manual. References to state personnel, agencies, and fees will be interpreted, where required, as meaning the City of LaFayette municipal equivalents.
(b) Protection of traffic and roadway. Unless specifically stated in the permit, no utility may occupy city rights-of-way unless sufficient space is available so that the free flow and safety of traffic and other capacity considerations are not unduly impaired and the installation does not prevent the department from reasonably maintaining the streets, structures, traffic control devices and other appurtenant facilities, and further provided that maintenance and operations of the facilities do not jeopardize the traffic, street structure, other users of the right-of-way or the right-of-way itself.
(c) Grading. If the grades or lines of any street within the city right-of-way are changed at any time by the city or by federal or state highway authorities during the term of the permit and this change involves an area in which the utility's facilities are located, then the utility must, at its own cost and expense and upon the request of the city upon reasonable notice, protect or promptly alter or relocate the facilities, or any part thereof, so as to conform with such new grades or lines. In the event the utility refuses or neglects to so protect, alter, or relocate all or part of the facilities, the city will have the right to break through, remove, alter, or relocate all or any part of the facilities without any liability to the utility, and the utility must pay to the city the costs incurred in connection with such breaking through, removal, alteration, or relocation.
(d) Installation of poles and other wire-holding structures and relocation. Unless otherwise provided in a valid service agreement, no placement of any pole or wire-holding structure of the utility is to be considered a vested interest in the right-of-way, and such poles or structures are to be removed, relocated underground, or modified by the utility at its own expense whenever the city determines that the public convenience would be enhanced thereby. The facilities must be so located and installed as to cause minimum interference with the rights and convenience of property owners.
(e) Utilities protection. As provided in O.C.G.A § 25-9-6 (the Georgia Utility Facility Protection Act) and other applicable state law currently in place or as amended, no utility may commence, perform, or engage in blasting or in excavating with mechanized excavating facilities unless and until the utility planning the blasting or excavating has given forty-eight (48) hours' notice by submitting a locate request to the utility protection center, beginning the next business day, as defined in O.C.G.A. § 25-9-3(3), after such notice is provided, excluding hours during days other than business days.
(Ord. No. 19-01, § 1, 1-14-2019)
977:

(a) Purpose. The city finds it is in the best interest of the city, including its residents and businesses, to establish requirements, specifications, and reasonable conditions regarding the siting of small wireless facilities in its public rights-of-way. These requirements, specifications, and reasonable conditions are adopted in order to protect the public health, safety, and welfare of the residents and businesses of the city and to reasonably manage and protect the city's public rights-of-way.
(b) Authority. O.C.G.A. § 32-4-92(a)(10) authorizes the city to establish reasonable regulations for the installation, construction, maintenance, renewal, removal, and relocation of pipes, mains, conduits, cables, wires, poles, towers, traffic and other signals, and other equipment, facilities, or appliances in, on, along, over, or under the public roads and streets of the city. Further, 47 U.S.C. § 253(c) provides that the city has authority to manage its public rights-of-way. Finally, the Georgia Streamlining Wireless Facilities and Antennas Act, O.C.G.A. Title 36, Chapter 66C (the "SWFAA"), addresses the placement of small wireless facilities in the city's public rights-of-way.
(c) Objective. The objective of this article is to:
(1) Implement the SWFAA, as it pertains to facilities and poles in the public rights-of-way not used for the supply or distribution of electric power by the city; and
(2) Ensure use of the public rights-of-way is consistent with the design, appearance and other features of nearby land uses, protects the integrity of historic, cultural and scenic resources and does not harm residents' quality of life.
(d) Scope. Though the city is exempt from the SWFAA as an "electric supplier," the city is voluntarily complying with the SWFAA only to the extent that it applies to facilities and poles in the public rights-of-way not deemed an "electric facility" under the provisions of the SWFAA. Any colocation of a small wireless facility with an electric facility in the city must comply with article VIII of chapter 19 of the LaFayette City Code.
(e) Definitions. For the purposes of this article, the following terms, phrases, words, and their derivations, regardless of whether capitalized or lowercase, have the following meanings:
(1) Antenna means communications equipment that transmits, receives, or transmits and receives electromagnetic radio frequency signals or surface waves used in the provision of wireless services or other wireless communications. This term does not include television broadcast antennas, antennas designed for amateur radio use, or satellite dishes for residential or household purposes.
(2) Applicable codes means uniform building, fire, safety, electrical, plumbing, or mechanical codes adopted by a recognized national code organization to the extent the codes have been adopted by the State of Georgia or the city or are otherwise applicable in the city.
(3) Applicant means any person that submits an application.
(4) Application means a written request submitted by an applicant to the city for a permit to collocate a small wireless facility in a right-of-way; or install, modify, or replace a pole or decorative pole in a right-of-way on which a small wireless facility is or will be located.
(5) Authority pole means a pole owned, managed, or operated by or on behalf of the city. This term does not include poles, support structures, electric transmission structures, or equipment of any type owned by the city in its capacity as an electric supplier.
(6) Collocate or collocation means to install, mount, modify, or replace a small wireless facility on or adjacent to a pole, decorative pole, or support structure.
(7) Consolidated application means an application for the collocation of multiple small wireless facilities on existing poles or support structures. or for the installation, modification, or replacement of multiple poles and the collocation of associated small wireless facilities.
(8) Decorative pole means an authority pole that is specially designed and placed for aesthetic purposes.
(9) Department means the city's public works department.
(10) Director means the director of the city's public works department.
(11) Electric supplier means any electric light and power company subject to regulation by the Georgia Public Service Commission, any electric membership corporation furnishing retail service in this state, and any municipality which furnishes service within this state. Since the city is an electric supplier, this article is inapplicable in all respects to city-owned electric system facilities, which is governed under article VIII of chapter 19 of the LaFayette City Code.
(12) Fee means a one-time, nonrecurring charge based on time and expense.
(13) Historic district means any:
a. District, site, building, structure, or object included in, or eligible for inclusion in, the National Register of Historic Places maintained by the secretary of the interior of the United States in accordance with section VI.D.1.a.i—v of the Nationwide Programmatic Agreement codified by 47 C.F.R. Part I;
b. Area designated as a historic district under Article 2 of Chapter 10 of Title 44, the Georgia Historic Preservation Act; or
c. Area designated as a historic district or property by law.
(14) Law means all federal, state, or local laws, statutes, common laws, codes, rules, regulations, orders, or ordinances.
(15) Permit means a written authorization, in electronic or hard copy format, required to be issued by the city to initiate, continue, or complete the collocation of a small wireless facility or the installation, modification, or replacement of a pole or decorative pole upon which a small wireless facility is collocated.
(16) Person means an individual, corporation, limited liability company, partnership, association, trust, or other entity or organization, including an authority.
(17) Pole means a vertical pole such as a utility, lighting, traffic, or similar pole made of wood, concrete, metal, or other material that is lawfully located or to be located within a right-of-way, including without limitation a replacement pole and an authority pole. This term does not include a support structure, decorative pole, or electric transmission structure.
(18) Rate means a recurring charge.
(19) Reconditioning means the activities associated with substantially painting, reconditioning, improving, or repairing authority poles.
(20) Replace or replacement means to replace a pole or decorative pole with a new pole or a new decorative pole, similar in design, size, and scale to the existing pole or decorative pole consistent with 47 C.F.R. § 1.40001(b)(7) as it existed on January 1, 2019, in order to address limitations of, or change requirements applicable to, the existing pole to structurally support the collocation of a small wireless facility.
(21) Right(s)-of-way means the surface and space in, on, above, within, over, below, under or through any real property in which the city has an interest in law or equity, whether held in fee, or other estate or interest, or as a trustee for the public, including, but not limited to, any public street, boulevard, road, highway, freeway, lane, alley, court, sidewalk, parkway, or any other place, area, or real property owned by or under the legal or equitable control of the city.
(22) Small wireless facility means radio transceivers; surface wave couplers; antennas; coaxial, fiber optic, or other cabling; power supply; backup batteries; and comparable and associated equipment, regardless of technological configuration, at a fixed location or fixed locations that enable communication or surface wave communication between user equipment and a communications network and that meet both of the following qualifications:
a. Each wireless provider's antenna could fit within an enclosure of no more than six (6) cubic feet in volume; and
b. All other wireless equipment associated with the facility is cumulatively no more than twenty-eight (28) cubic feet in volume, measured based upon the exterior dimensions of height by width by depth of any enclosure that may be used.
The following types of associated ancillary equipment are not included in the calculation of the volume of all other wireless equipment associated with any such facility: electric meters; concealment elements; telecommunications demarcation boxes; grounding equipment; power transfer switches; cut-off switches; and vertical cable runs for connection of power and other services. This term does not include a pole, decorative pole, or support structure on, under, or within which the equipment is located or collocated or to which the equipment is attached and does not include any wireline backhaul facilities or coaxial, fiber optic, or other cabling that is between small wireless facilities, poles, decorative poles, or support structures or that is not otherwise immediately adjacent to or directly associated with a particular antenna.
(23) State means the State of Georgia.
(24) Support structure means a building, billboard, water tank, or any other structure to which a small wireless facility is or may be attached. This term does not include a decorative pole, electric transmission structure, or pole.
(25) SWFAA means the Georgia Streamlining Wireless Facilities and Antennas Act, as codified in O.C.G.A. Title 36, Chapter 66C.
(26) Wireless infrastructure provider means any person, including a person authorized to provide telecommunications services in this state, that builds, installs, or operates small wireless facilities, poles, decorative poles, or support structures on which small wireless facilities are or are intended to be used for collocation but that is not a wireless services provider.
(27) Wireless provider means a wireless infrastructure provider or a wireless services provider.
(28) Wireless services means any services provided to the public using licensed or unlicensed spectrum, including the use of Wi-Fi, whether at a fixed location or mobile.
(29) Wireless services provider means a person that provides wireless services.
(30) Wireline backhaul facility means an aboveground or underground wireline facility used to transport communications data from a telecommunications demarcation box associated with small wireless facility to a network.
If any federal or state law containing definitions used in this article is amended, the definition in the referenced section, as amended, controls.
(Ord. No. 19-07, § 1, 9-30-2019)

(a) Purpose. The city finds it is in the best interest of the city, including its residents, businesses, and electric service customers, to establish requirements, specifications, and reasonable conditions regarding the siting of small wireless facilities on electric supplier facilities, as that term is defined in this article. These requirements, specifications, and conditions are adopted in order to protect the public health, safety and welfare of the residents, businesses, and electric service customers of the city and to reasonably manage and protect the city's electrical facilities.

(1) Provide for the reasonable attachment of any equipment (as defined herein below) to electric facilities in the city; and

As such, the city installs, maintains, operates, and owns electric supplier facilities as defined in this article. The scope of this article thus governs all siting of small wireless facilities upon all electric supplier facilities in the city's rights-of-way.

Engineering includes design, proper conductor spacing and bonding, calculations to determine proper ground clearances and pole down guy and anchor strength requirements for horizontal and transverse loading, and compliance with all applicable requirements. Also included among make ready costs are the costs of installing or changing out primary poles, secondary poles and drop and lift poles, including the cost of installation and/or removal of guys, anchors, stub poles, materials and equipment, temporary construction and all other construction in accordance with the technical requirements and specifications as required by the city. City make ready costs must be verifiably comparable to the cost the city pays for similar make ready work to its own facilities.
(5) Pole means a wooden, concrete or steel structure owned, controlled, or otherwise operated by the city to support distribution lines and related facilities of the city, including drop, lift, light poles and streetlight poles that do not support distribution lines and related facilities.

Except as otherwise provided in this article, a sidewalk café operating in the city must comply with the following conditions and regulations:
(1) Pedestrian clearance. A minimum area of no less than five (5) feet in width must be reserved at all times for continuous unobstructed pedestrian traffic along the public sidewalk. This reserved area must not be encroached upon even if it precludes the operation of a sidewalk café. Additionally, a minimum of one (1) foot of unobstructed space must be reserved at all times between any sidewalk café perimeter and the nearest obstacle, including, but not limited to, streetscape elements and the curb.
(2) Limitation on area. The area in which a sidewalk café is operated must abut the outside front wall of the restaurant of which it is an extension and must not extend in either direction beyond the outside front wall of the restaurant.
(3) Furnishings. Furnishings must not be secured to lamp posts, streetlights, trees or any other public street fixtures. Furnishings may not be stacked or stored outside on the public right-of-way at any time.
a. Fences. A system of connected posts and railing, firmly secured, but temporarily moveable, must be placed to maintain the boundaries of the sidewalk café. Fence materials should be discreet in color, design, materials, and finishes, and relatively transparent. Fences must not obstruct visibility to pedestrians on the sidewalk nor obstruct driver visibility for vehicular traffic.
b. Tables and chairs. Tables and chairs must match and be made of safe, sturdy, and durable material, such as wood, steel, wrought iron, or high-density plastic. All furniture must be commercial grade and manufactured for outdoor commercial use. Small round or square tables must seat no more than four (4) people. Use of larger tables may be granted provided that all clearance requirements are met. Round tables must be no larger than three (3) feet in diameter. Square tables must be no larger than three (3) feet wide and rectangular tables no more than three (3) by four (4) feet. Tables must be no more than thirty (30) inches in height.
c. Umbrellas. Each table may be equipped with an umbrella that, when open, must extend to at least the same diameter as the table it serves and must be anchored with a weighted base. Any umbrella protruding into public space must be positioned at a minimum height of seven (7) feet. An umbrella may not display the name or logo of the restaurant operating the sidewalk café nor advertise a product. Each umbrella must be maintained in good, clean, and operable condition.
d. Menu boards and signs. Menu boards, both portable and on walls, must comply with all applicable city code requirements.
e. Trash receptacles. The number, type, and location of trash receptables is subject to approval by the city.
(4) Landscaping. Flower boxes or planters may be used to define the corner boundaries of the seating area of the sidewalk café. The combined height of the planters and live plants must not exceed four (4) feet from sidewalk grade and must be no wider than two (2) feet at the base. The planting areas must be planted with seasonal blooming or ornamental evergreen live plants year round. The permit holder must maintain flower boxes and planting areas. The flower boxes and planters must be portable and made of safe, durable, and attractive materials such as wood, steel, colored concrete, or high-density plastic.
(5) Alcoholic beverages/open containers. Sidewalk café permit holders are exempt from the restrictions on open containers if such establishment is otherwise licensed to sell alcoholic beverages under the applicable state laws and ordinances of the city. All applicable provisions of chapter 4 (Alcoholic Beverages) of the LaFayette City Code and title 3 (Alcoholic Beverages) of the official Code of Georgia will be enforced regarding the sale, service, possession, and consumption of alcoholic beverages. The permit holder must post approved signs designating the limits of the open container area.
(6) Divider required. At restaurants where alcohol is served, the area permitted for a sidewalk café must be separated from the remaining sidewalk area by a system of connected posts and railing that serves to contain crowds and maintain the boundaries of the cafe. The system must be designed and constructed such that it resists movement but can be disassembled and removed, if necessary. The design must be included in the application and must be approved by the city's codes department prior to issuance of a permit. Such divider must not be less than three (3) feet (thirty-six (36) inches) nor more than three (3) feet six (6) inches (forty-two (42) inches) in height. All tables and chairs must be located totally within the limits of the divider. It is the responsibility of the permit holder to maintain the divider in its exact approved location at all times.
(7) Sanitation. It is the responsibility and duty of the restaurant to which the sidewalk café permit is issued to maintain the area covered by the permit in a clean, neat, and orderly manner at all times. The area must be cleared of all debris at all times. All tables and chairs must be kept clean, sanitary, safe, and in structurally sound condition at all times.
(8) Hours of operation. A business with a sidewalk café permit may be open for breakfast, lunch, and dinner, or any combination thereof, consistent with the normal hours of operation of the restaurant.
(9) Smoking. Smoking, as that term is defined under section 12-70 of the LaFayette City Code, is prohibited within sidewalk cafés.
(10) Removal of furnishings and suspension of operation. The city may require, from time to time, that tables, chairs, dividers, or other furnishings be removed from the public sidewalk area and that outside operations be suspended as required by the city for sidewalk cleaning or maintenance or for such other purposes as the city may determine, in its sole discretion, as necessary. Such purposes may include, but are not limited to, the following:
a. Any permitted special event;
b. Any street, sidewalk, or utility construction;
c. Any emergency situations; or
d. Any event necessitating removal for the protection of the public health, safety, and welfare.
(Ord. No. 22/04, § 1, 5-9-2022)

For purposes of this chapter, the following terms, phrases, words, and their derivations shall have the meanings set forth in this section, unless the context clearly indicates that another meaning is intended. When not inconsistent with the context, words used in the present tense include the future, words used in the plural number include the singular number, and words used in the singular number include the plural number.
Affiliated person means each person who falls into one (1) or more of the following categories: (1) each person having, directly or indirectly, a controlling interest in the applicant; (2) each person in which the applicant has, directly or indirectly, a controlling interest; (3) each officer, director, joint venturer or joint venture partner, of the applicant; and (4) each person, directly or indirectly, controlling, controlled by, or under common control with, the applicant; provided that "affiliated person" shall in no event mean the city or any creditor of the applicant solely by virtue of its status as a creditor and which is not otherwise an affiliated person by reason of owning a controlling interest in, being owned by, or being under common ownership, common management or common control with, the applicant.
Cable services means "cable services" as defined in the Communications Act of 1934, as amended by the Cable Communications Policy Act of 1984, the Cable Television Consumer Protection and Competition Act of 1992, the Telecommunications Act of 1996, and as may be further amended from time to time (the "Cable Act"), but does not include telecommunications services or private telecommunications services. In the event that "cable services" is no longer defined in the Cable Act or the definition in the Cable Act otherwise becomes inapplicable, "Cable services" shall mean "cable services" as defined in the Cable Act immediately prior to such term no longer being defined in the Cable Act or such definition otherwise becoming inapplicable.
Cable system means any "cable system" as defined in the Cable Act.
City means the City of LaFayette, Georgia.
City council means the city council of the city and its designee or any successor thereto.
Control or controlling interest means the possession, directly or indirectly, of the power to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies of a person, including, but not limited to, a person's compliance with a franchise or revocable license, whether through the ownership of voting securities, by contract, or otherwise, and the beneficial ownership of shares representing ten (10) percent or more of the votes entitled to be cast by a corporation's voting shares shall create a rebuttable presumption of control.
Facility services means the installation, construction, operation or maintenance of conduit or related facilities in the streets by a person for sale or lease to third parties, other than affiliated persons, that use such conduit or related facilities for the transmission of telecommunication services, but such person does not itself provide telecommunications service or cable service to such third parties or any locations or other persons in the license area.
Franchise means an initial authorization, or renewal thereof, issued by the city in accordance with the provisions of this chapter, which authorizes the occupation and use of the streets by a telecommunications system to provide telecommunications services.
Grantee means the legal entity to which is granted the right, authority and responsibility to provide facility services along licensed routes pursuant to a license, or to construct, install, operate and maintain a telecommunications system as necessary to: (a) furnish, supply and distribute telecommunications services to any locations or persons in the franchise or license area; (b) provide private telecommunications services along licensed routes pursuant to a license; or (c) transport telecommunications services across the city along licensed routes pursuant to a license without terminating or originating any telecommunications services at or from any person or location in the city.
May is permissive.
Ordinance means this chapter and all modifications and amendments thereto.
Person means any individual or any association, firm, partnership, joint venture, corporation or other legally recognized entity, whether for profit or not for profit, but shall not mean the city.
Private telecommunications services means the transmission of telecommunications by a person, regardless of the facilities used, for or in connection with the internal operations of such person's business, residence or employment and not for or in connection with the provision or offering of telecommunications services for sale or resale to any person, and shall not mean cable services.
Revocable license means an initial authorization or renewal thereof, issued by the city in accordance with the provisions of this chapter, which authorizes the occupation and use of specifically identified streets, provided that a revocable license shall be issued only in the limited circumstances set forth in subsection 20.5-21(a).
Shall is mandatory, not merely directive.
Streets means the surface of, as well as the spaces above and below, any and all streets, alleyways, avenues, highways, boulevards, driveways, bridges, tunnels, parks, parkways, public grounds or waters, and other public rights-of-way within or belonging to the city.
Telecommunications means "telecommunications" as defined by 47 U. S.C. § 153(43) of the Communications Act of 1934, as amended by the Telecommunications Act of 1996, but shall not include cable services.
Telecommunications service means "telecommunications service" as defined by 47 U.S.C. § 153(46) of the Communications Act of 1934, as amended by the Telecommunications Act of 1996, but shall not include cable services. In the event that "telecommunications service" is no longer defined in the Communications Act or the definition in the Communications Act otherwise becomes inapplicable, "telecommunications service" shall mean "telecommunications service" as defined in the Communications Act immediately prior to such term no longer being defined in the Communications Act or such definition otherwise becoming inapplicable.
Telecommunications system means the system, plant, equipment or property within the streets in the franchise or license area over which telecommunications service or private telecommunications service is provided, and to be constructed, operated, and maintained by a grantee pursuant to a franchise or license ordinance or agreement.
(Ord. No. 01-09, § 1.1, 9-10-2001)
